target_customer: Banks, card providers, travel platforms and payment firms that white-label VAT reclaim for travellers; travellers and businesses claiming VAT back
problem: Travellers and businesses leave most reclaimable VAT unclaimed because refund schemes are slow, paper based and take high commissions from reclaim merchants.
business_model: B2B2C white-label API and portal sold to banks and card issuers, revenue from a share of refunds
product_category: VAT reclaim API and fintech infrastructure

founders.name: Shawn Du
previous_startups: Two earlier startups, both exited per his own interview (names not given)
founders.background_notes: Employers and prior startups from a January 2026 Pulse 2.0 interview; education not found. FF News says the founders met at Imperial College London, but no other co-founder is named in the sources opened.

competitors.name: UTU
competitors.what: Singapore based digital tax refund app for tourists in Europe, promising higher refunds than the incumbent operators
competitors.traction_then: Launched its Italy product in November 2019

competitors.name: Global Blue and Premier Tax Free (now Planet)
competitors.what: Incumbent in store tax refund operators that the UTU article names as the status quo
competitors.traction_then: Dominant incumbents; tourists reportedly received about 55 to 60 percent of the VAT

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs invoice capture and OCR, integration with bank apps and card networks, and filing with tax authorities in several countries; standard engineering with hard regulatory plumbing.

defensibility.rationale: Bank integrations and tax authority relationships create some lock in, but the core idea of digital refund filing was being copied by UTU, Zapptax and Pie VAT.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat move by incumbents found in the sources opened.

market_need_then: Revenir's own site says about 80 percent of VAT goes unclaimed and reclaim merchants charge over 30 percent commission; the CEO says he hit the pain personally.

branding.domain_note: Uses revenir.ai; an earlier related domain userevenir.com appears in a directory. No purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B fintech voice, trust and bank partner focus

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, no community or mascot found; coverage is about the product only.

outcome_analysis: Revenir is still operating after YC Winter 2020, selling a white-label VAT reclaim API to banks and card providers. Sources show a seed round in February 2024 and a CEO interview in January 2026, but no large round or exit, so it looks like a slow, partner driven fintech that has not yet shown clear breakout traction.
notes: Funding unverified in detail: CB Insights lists $3.65M over 3 rounds with a $3.15M seed on 2024-02-19 and Palm Drive Capital; trade press says 2.5M GBP raised from shareholders. Amounts conflict by currency so the seed amount is left null; the aggregator figures are not adopted as a round amount. Founding year sources conflict (2019 vs 2021). Earlier rounds before 2024 not found. Competitor search found Zapptax (2018) and Pie VAT but without dated sources, so they are not listed.
